executive_summary: The client seeks a claims processing platform to reduce FNOL to adjuster assignment time and misrouted claims percentage. The proposed solution includes document ingestion, classification, extraction, triage, and AI-driven fraud detection, with operational dashboards for monitoring KPIs. Key risks include meeting the deadline while ensuring adequate lead time, achieving security compliance particularly regarding data residency, avoiding new dependencies during integration, securing board approval for large purchases, and managing data deletion vs retention policies.

requirements.title: Reduce FNOL to adjuster assignment time
requirements.description: Reduce average time from FNOL to correct adjuster assignment under 4 working hours.
requirements.source_quote: Reduce the average time from FNOL to correct adjuster assignment from 3.8 working days to under 4 working hours for straightforward claims.

requirements.title: Reduce misrouted claims percentage
requirements.description: Reduce misrouted claims from 22% to below 5%.
requirements.source_quote: Reduce misrouted claims from 22% to below 5%.

requirements.source_quote: Give adjusters a concise, trustworthy summary of each claim so they can start assessment without opening every attachment.

requirements.title: Detect potential fraud
requirements.description: Improve early detection of potentially fraudulent claims by surfacing anomalies to SIU.
requirements.source_quote: Improve early detection of potentially fraudulent claims by surfacing anomalies to the Special Investigations Unit (SIU), without automatically declining any claim.

requirements.title: Ingest claim documents
requirements.description: Ingestion of claim documents from all four lodgement channels is in scope.
requirements.source_quote: - Ingestion of claim documents from all four lodgement channels.

requirements.title: Document classification and extraction
requirements.description: Document classification, data extraction and claim summarisation is in scope.
requirements.source_quote: - Document classification, data extraction and claim summarisation.

requirements.source_quote: - Triage: complexity scoring, line-of-business routing and adjuster queue assignment.

requirements.source_quote: - Fraud-indicator flagging for referral to SIU.

requirements.description: The solution shall ingest claim documents from the web portal, mobile app, monitored email inboxes and scanned paper batches, and associate every document with the correct claim number in ClaimsNet.
requirements.source_quote: The solution shall ingest claim documents from the web portal, mobile app, monitored email inboxes and scanned paper batches, and associate every document with the correct claim number in ClaimsNet.

requirements.source_quote: The solution shall extract key fields from claim forms, police reports, repair estimates and invoices, including at minimum: policy number, incident date, incident location, vehicle registration (motor), third-party details, itemised amounts and totals.

requirements.source_quote: The solution shall generate a plain-language summary of each claim (no more than 200 words) for the assigned adjuster, highlighting the incident, the parties involved, amounts claimed and any missing documents.

requirements.title: Every factual statement in the summary must be
requirements.description: Every factual statement in the summary must be traceable to a source document.
requirements.source_quote: Every factual statement in the summary must be traceable to a source document.

requirements.title: Assign complexity score

requirements.source_quote: The solution shall assign each claim a complexity score and route it to the appropriate line-of-business queue and adjuster tier, using rules configurable by Corvane's claims operations team without vendor involvement.

requirements.title: Identify fraud indicators
requirements.description: Identify potential fraud in claims.
requirements.source_quote: The solution shall identify potential fraud indicators (for example, inconsistent dates, duplicate invoices across claims, altered documents) and refer flagged claims to SIU with an explanation.

requirements.title: No automatic claim closure

requirements.source_quote: The solution must never automatically decline or close a claim.

approach.summary: Develop a claims processing platform that integrates document ingestion, classification, extraction, triage, and AI-driven fraud detection.
components: Machine Learning Models for Classification and Fraud Detection
approach.rationale: This approach covers all must-priority requirements while leveraging modern technologies for efficiency and scalability.

approach.summary: Combine document ingestion from web portal, mobile app, email, and paper batches into a single component to avoid redundancy.
approach.rationale: This consolidation reduces complexity and ensures consistent data handling across all channels.

approach.summary: Develop a document ingestion service that extracts key fields from various claim documents, handling low-quality inputs and flagging unreadable ones.
approach.rationale: Reuses existing IBM MQ for integration with the DMS, ensuring compatibility with legacy systems and data protection constraints.

approach.summary: Implement a summarization module that generates claim summaries based on extracted facts, ensuring all factual statements are verifiable.
approach.rationale: Uses existing metadata from ClaimsNet to maintain accuracy and avoid data duplication, aligning with the client's need for precision in claims processing.

approach.summary: Integrate a machine learning model to assign complexity scores to claims based on extracted fields.
approach.rationale: Leverages existing document taxonomy and IBM MQ for seamless data flow, ensuring the solution is scalable with minimal impact on legacy systems.

approach.summary: Deploy a fraud detection module that identifies potential fraudulent claims by analyzing extracted fields.
approach.rationale: Uses existing document management system for data access, ensuring the solution is compliant with data protection regulations and legacy constraints.

approach.summary: Ensure no automatic claim closure; all decisions require human review.
approach.rationale: Maintains control over claims closure process to ensure accuracy and compliance with internal policies.

approach.summary: Allow for manual corrections during the review process to improve model accuracy.
approach.rationale: Facilitates continuous improvement of AI models through human feedback, enhancing overall system performance.

approach.summary: Automate claim classification using AI-generated labels based on extracted fields.
approach.rationale: Enhances operational efficiency by reducing manual intervention in the claims processing workflow.

approach.summary: Capture corrections for model improvement and draft missing information requests to ensure completeness of claims data.
approach.rationale: Supports ongoing model training and ensures comprehensive claim records, aligning with client's need for continuous improvement.

approach.summary: Provide operational dashboards to monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) related to claims processing.
approach.rationale: Enables real-time monitoring and analysis of claims data, supporting informed decision-making and process optimization.

approach.summary: Develop a routing decision explanation module that provides business-friendly explanations for claims processing decisions.
approach.rationale: This aligns with Corvane's need to explain routing decisions in business terms, ensuring adjusters and leadership can justify actions to customers or regulators.

approach.summary: Implement a load balancer and auto-scaling group to ensure peak throughput and 99.5% availability.
approach.rationale: Automates scaling based on demand, ensuring performance without manual intervention.

approach.summary: Schedule maintenance during off-peak hours to minimize impact on service availability.
approach.rationale: Ensures minimal disruption to users and critical operations.

approach.summary: Automate document ingestion from email and portal channels, ensuring read access to policy coverage details.
approach.rationale: Reuses existing interfaces, avoiding changes to the core system the client wants untouched.

approach.summary: Implement a manual fallback mechanism for resilience in case of service failure.
approach.rationale: Provides a reliable backup plan that can be manually triggered if needed.

approach.summary: Ensure WCAG 2.1 AA compliance, version control for models and prompts, and delete working copies within 30 days.
approach.rationale: Meets accessibility standards and manages data lifecycle efficiently.

approach.summary: Implement a quality evaluation framework to model and run evaluations both pre-go-live and post-handover.
approach.rationale: Combines NFR-14 and NFR-15 into one component for efficiency, ensuring consistent evaluation processes throughout the project lifecycle.

approach.summary: Implement single sign-on (SSO) and role-based access control.
approach.rationale: SSO simplifies user authentication, while RBAC ensures secure data access based on roles.

approach.summary: Store data in a Malaysia-based cloud service to meet data residency requirements.
approach.rationale: Complies with local regulations and minimizes latency for users in the region.

approach.summary: Minimize exposure of personal data through role-based access control and secure APIs.
approach.rationale: Reduces unauthorized access to sensitive information.

approach.summary: Ensure audit logs are immutable and retained for compliance purposes.
approach.rationale: Maintains a record of all actions taken on the system for auditing and regulatory requirements.

approach.summary: Schedule annual security testing to identify and mitigate vulnerabilities.
approach.rationale: Regularly assesses the security posture of the system to ensure compliance with best practices.

approach.summary: Remediate high or critical findings from security assessments promptly.
approach.rationale: Ensures that significant security issues are addressed in a timely manner to prevent breaches.

approach.summary: Support the model risk management process by documenting and monitoring models.
approach.rationale: Facilitates compliance with regulatory requirements for managing financial risks.

approach.summary: Disclose third-party models used in the system to relevant stakeholders.
approach.rationale: Ensures transparency and accountability regarding the use of external models.

approach.summary: Ensure personnel handling production data have appropriate security clearances.
approach.rationale: Protects sensitive information from unauthorized access by ensuring staff are vetted properly.

approach.rationale: Reuses existing interfaces, avoiding changes to the core system the client wants untouched.

approach.rationale: Maintains consistency with current practices, reducing risk of errors or misconfigurations.

approach.summary: Integrate document storage into the DMS system following the client's data residency requirements.

approach.summary: Authenticate users through Active Directory to ensure secure access control.

risks.title: Deadline vs lead time
risks.description: The fixed pilot go-live date of 30 June 2027 conflicts with the hardware procurement timeline, which typically takes 16 to 20 weeks from purchase order.
risks.mitigation: Agree an interim approved hosting option for the pilot or re-baseline the date at contract award.

risks.title: Deletion vs retention
risks.description: There is a potential conflict between NFR-12, which requires deleting working copies within 30 days, and NFR-13, which states that SIU document requirements may necessitate retaining certain documents for longer periods.
risks.mitigation: Clarify with the client how long working copies must be retained and ensure compliance with both NFR-12 and NFR-13.

risks.title: Ambiguity: Real-time targets
risks.description: The terms 'real time' in NFR-02 and NFR-04 are not quantified, which could lead to disputes over the system's performance.
risks.mitigation: Define clear metrics for 'real time' in both requirements to avoid misunderstandings.

risks.title: Security compliance: Data residency
risks.description: The requirement that all customer data must be stored and processed within Corvane's Malaysian data centres (SEC-02) may conflict with the need for peak throughput and 99.5% availability, as local storage might limit performance.
risks.mitigation: Evaluate the impact of data residency on system performance and explore potential solutions such as edge computing or hybrid cloud strategies.

risks.title: Integration: Avoiding new dependencies
risks.description: The requirement to avoid new dependencies on nightly SFTP batch interfaces (INT-07 and INT-08) may conflict with the need for peak throughput, as manual fallback options could impact performance.
risks.mitigation: Assess the feasibility of alternative integration methods that do not rely on SFTP interfaces and ensure they meet the required performance standards.

risks.title: Commercial: Board approval for large purchases
risks.description: The requirement to assume typical procurement time (COM-04) may conflict with the need for a fixed price pilot phase, as delays in obtaining Board approval could impact project timelines.
risks.mitigation: Provide a detailed timeline that accounts for potential delays in obtaining Board approval and include contingency plans in the bid proposal.

assumptions.statement: The exact number of document types in Corvane's taxonomy will be provided after contract award.
assumptions.rationale: To ensure accurate classification, we need the complete taxonomy.

assumptions.statement: Corvane's claims operations team can configure routing rules without vendor involvement.
assumptions.rationale: This allows for flexibility and local optimization of claim processing workflows.

assumptions.statement: The document taxonomy will be provided after contract award.
assumptions.rationale: Ensures alignment with client's specific needs without premature assumptions.

assumptions.statement: The complexity scoring and fraud detection models are third-party solutions.
assumptions.rationale: Allows for leveraging existing, proven technologies while maintaining compliance with data protection constraints.

assumptions.statement: The team will include a named delivery lead and solution architect who will remain on the engagement through full motor rollout.
assumptions.rationale: Ensures continuity and alignment with Corvane's expectations for key personnel.

assumptions.statement: Corvane's data science team will run evaluations after handover to measure model quality.
assumptions.rationale: Meets the client's need for ongoing quality assurance without duplicating effort.

assumptions.statement: Off-peak hours are defined as 2 AM - 6 AM local time
assumptions.rationale: RFP does not specify exact off-peak hours, so we assume a common timeframe.

assumptions.statement: Maintenance tasks can be automated using existing tools and scripts.
assumptions.rationale: Automation is assumed to reduce manual effort while maintaining compliance with the client's constraints.

open_questions.question: What is the target time for claim assignment?
open_questions.reason: The current average time (3.8 working days) is context, not a requirement.

open_questions.question: What are the specific document types that must be handled by the platform?
open_questions.reason: While it mentions several document types, there's no explicit statement of what must be included in the solution.

open_questions.question: How should claims be classified and triaged?
open_questions.reason: The method or criteria for classification and triage are not specified.

open_questions.question: What is the expected reduction in adjuster time spent on reading documents?
open_questions.reason: While 40% of their time is mentioned, there's no target stated.

open_questions.question: How should customer satisfaction be improved according to the RFP?
open_questions.reason: The current and desired levels of customer satisfaction are not quantified.

open_questions.question: What is the definition of 'straightforward claims'?
open_questions.reason: The term 'straightforward claims' is not defined in the RFP.

open_questions.question: What are the data protection constraints in section 8?
open_questions.reason: The quote mentions data protection constraints but does not specify them.

open_questions.question: What is the taxonomy of document types?
open_questions.reason: The number of document types (27) is mentioned but not detailed.

open_questions.question: What specific metrics should the operational dashboards cover?
open_questions.reason: The RFP mentions volumes, processing times, routing accuracy, extraction accuracy and adjuster override rates but does not specify these as requirements.

open_questions.question: What is the exact context for claims in ClaimsNet that must be loaded when accessing the solution?
open_questions.reason: The RFP states that the solution should appear inside or be reachable from the ClaimsNet claim screen, but it does not provide details on what specific context needs to be loaded.

open_questions.question: What is the exact definition of 'degradation beyond NFR-1 targets'?
open_questions.reason: The quote does not specify what constitutes degradation.

open_questions.question: What specific actions must be taken for high or critical findings from security testing?
open_questions.reason: The quote mentions remediation but does not specify the exact steps.

open_questions.question: Is there a specific timeline for when the solution should undergo initial penetration testing?
open_questions.reason: While it is mentioned that testing must be done before go-live, no specific date or time frame is provided.

open_questions.question: What is the definition of 'working copies'?
open_questions.reason: The term 'working copies' is not defined in the RFP.

open_questions.question: What constitutes an 'exceptionally strong justification' for a later pilot date?
open_questions.reason: The criteria for what qualifies as an exceptionally strong justification are not specified.

open_questions.question: What are the specific measurable outcomes for payment milestones?
open_questions.reason: The RFP mentions measurable outcomes but does not specify what they are.

open_questions.question: What is the expected level of detail for client references?
open_questions.reason: The RFP mentions providing client references but does not specify the required level of detail.

open_questions.question: How will 'drift' be defined and measured?
open_questions.reason: While drift detection is mentioned, there is no clear definition or measurement criteria provided.

open_questions.question: How will the system handle data that needs to be retained for SIU investigations but must also be deleted within 30 days?
open_questions.reason: To ensure compliance with both NFR-12 and NFR-13.

open_questions.question: What specific metrics should be used to define 'real time' in NFR-02 and NFR-04?
open_questions.reason: To avoid disputes over the system's performance.

issues.feedback: These must-priority requirements are not addressed by any approach item: COM-11. Add them to the relevant items.
FR-12 and FR-13 are redundant as they both address document classification and extraction, with only minor differences in scope.
The approach for FR-05 (Ingest claim documents) and FR-11 (Ingest claim documents from the web portal, mobile) should be combined into a single component to avoid redundancy.
There is no risk related to the tension between NFR-06 (99.5% availability) and TL-02 (Full rollout by specified dates). This should be added to ensure both are considered.
FR-19 and FR-20 have similar content but different wording. Consider consolidating them for clarity.
The approach for NFR-14 (Model quality evaluation before go-live) and NFR-15 (Run evaluations post-handover) should be combined into a single component to avoid redundancy.
FR-12 and FR-13 are redundant as they both address document classification, with only minor differences in scope.
The approach violates the constraint of storing data in Malaysia (SEC-02) by proposing a cloud storage solution that may not be based in Malaysia.
There is an obvious tension between NFR-05 (peak throughput) and SEC-08 (annual security testing), which could impact the system's availability. This risk should be explicitly addressed.
FR-26 is marked as 'must' but its title and description are incomplete, which could lead to misinterpretation.
The approach does not explicitly address the requirement of no automatic claim closure (FR-19), even though it mentions a human review workflow.
